the functional resilience of microbial communities to multiple stressors depends on the disturbance history.

the question of whether the resilience of microbial communities to multiple stressors is influenced by the community disturbance history.
the effects of multiple anthropogenic stressors and their history on microbial communities in stream ecosystems, which are of high relevance for the functioning of ecosystems.
the ecological consequences of agricultural intensification on the resilience of microbial communities and their functions in aquatic ecosystems.

history matters, as microbial community responses to multiple stressors may be modified over time, and this should be considered when predicting the consequences of global change.
microbial communities are able to adapt to stressors and that these adaptions may be beneficial for the ecosystem.

the history of a microbial community matters for its resilience to multiple stressors and the maintenance of ecosystem functions.
